purpose: Provider-neutral jurisdiction/compliance research baseline; not personalized legal advice.

owner_jurisdiction.rule: Do not infer residence, nationality, citizenship, tax residency, entity domicile, professional-client status or account eligibility from ChatGPT/account/network/location metadata.

operating_model.current: private owner/team research platform; no public SaaS, no client asset custody, no copy trading, no brokerage service
operating_model.note: Whether the project itself triggers licensing depends on actual activity, client/service model, entity and jurisdiction. P01-D only defines evidence requirements.

jurisdictions.label: European Union / EEA baseline
regulator_sources: national competent authority TBD by owner/entity jurisdiction

facts: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA) establishes uniform requirements for crypto-asset service providers and applies to persons/undertakings providing crypto-asset services in the Union.
MiCA authorization is service-specific and supervised by the competent authority of the home Member State, with Union-wide validity subject to the regulation.
P01-D does not conclude that private own-account spot crypto trading requires CASP authorization; that depends on activity/service facts.

ESMA's CFD product-intervention framework introduced retail protections including leverage limits, margin close-out, negative balance protection, inducement restrictions and standardized risk warnings.

The historical ESMA limits include 30:1 for major FX pairs, 20:1 for non-major FX/gold/major indices, 10:1 for other commodities/non-major indices, 5:1 for equities/other reference values and 2:1 for cryptocurrencies.
Current binding implementation must be verified with the applicable national competent authority and provider terms at account-opening time.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: Identify specific Member State/EEA state and client classification before any broker/provider eligibility decision.

jurisdictions.label: United States baseline

facts: CFTC rules regulate off-exchange retail foreign-currency transactions.
Persons acting as counterparties to retail forex transactions generally must fall within permitted/regulated categories; CFTC rules include RFED and FCM registration structures.
17 CFR Part 5 is the primary current CFTC regulation set for off-exchange foreign currency transactions.
CFTC materials state that certain leveraged, margined or financed retail commodity transactions may be required to trade on registered venues absent an exception or relief.
Digital-asset regulatory treatment is product-specific and can involve CFTC and/or SEC authority; P01-D does not classify any specific token/product for U.S. law.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: U.S. person/resident/entity status and exact product/venue must be explicitly verified before eligibility.

jurisdictions.label: United Kingdom baseline

facts: FCA PS20/10 prohibits marketing, distribution and sale in or from the UK to retail clients of derivatives and ETNs referencing certain unregulated transferable cryptoassets.
The ban took effect on 6 January 2021.
FCA PS19/18 and COBS 22.5 apply retail protections to CFDs and leveraged rolling spot forex.
Protections include leverage limits, 50% margin close-out, negative balance protection, inducement restrictions and standardized risk warnings.
FCA Handbook COBS 22.5 sets 3.33% minimum margin for major FX pairs (about 30:1) and 5% for minor FX pairs/gold (about 20:1).

jurisdictions.owner_gate: UK retail/professional classification and provider authorization must be verified before product eligibility.

jurisdictions.label: Australia baseline

facts: ASIC's CFD product-intervention order applies retail-client protections including leverage limits from 30:1 to 2:1, margin close-out and negative balance protection.
ASIC extended the order through 23 May 2027 unless revoked or remade earlier.
ASIC's 2026 review states the order is due to expire in May 2027 unless remade, so status must be revalidated before use.
ASIC describes CFDs as potentially referencing FX, indices, equities, commodities or crypto-assets; exact product/provider authorization requires current validation.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: Australian retail/wholesale client status and provider authorization must be verified.

jurisdictions.label: Japan baseline

facts: FSA materials describe registration requirements for crypto-asset exchange service providers.
Crypto-asset derivatives are regulated under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act.
FSA materials describe a minimum 50% margin requirement for retail crypto-asset CFD transactions, corresponding to a 2:1 leverage ceiling.
FSA materials treat FX/derivative intermediaries under financial instruments regulation; exact current retail FX leverage and provider status must be verified at execution-provider selection.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: Japanese resident/entity and client status plus FSA registration of the venue/intermediary must be verified.

jurisdictions.label: Singapore baseline

facts: MAS PS-G03 sets consumer-protection expectations for Digital Payment Token service providers.
For retail customers, the guidelines restrict credit/leverage and DPT derivative facilitation, including leveraged DPT transactions and DPT derivatives contracts.
MAS states that a company must hold a Capital Markets Services licence to conduct regulated activities under the Securities and Futures Act unless exempt.
Capital-markets products include OTC derivatives, exchange-traded derivatives and spot foreign exchange for leveraged foreign exchange trading.
Licensed broker-dealers offering CFDs or leveraged spot FX are required to collect margins.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: Singapore retail/accredited/institutional status and provider licence/exemption must be verified.

jurisdictions.label: Dubai (VARA jurisdiction; excludes DIFC)

facts: VARA states that entities carrying out VA Activities by way of business in Dubai must be authorized/licensed unless exempt.
VARA's framework covers Dubai mainland and free zones except DIFC.
An entity actively investing its own portfolio in virtual assets at or above USD 250,000,000 equivalent during any rolling 30-day period must register with VARA.
VARA states that proprietary-portfolio registration does not itself authorize VA service activities or use of third-party assets.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: Determine whether any UAE activity is in Dubai/VARA, DIFC, ADGM or another emirate/federal regime before eligibility analysis.

jurisdictions.label: Hong Kong baseline

facts: SFC states that centralized virtual-asset trading platforms carrying on business in Hong Kong or actively marketing to Hong Kong investors are required to be licensed under the applicable SFO/AMLO regimes.
The current VATP licensing handbook requires licensed-platform compliance and emphasizes jurisdiction-specific compliance for activities outside Hong Kong.
SFC identifies Type 3 as leveraged foreign exchange trading and states that regulated activities generally require licensing unless an exemption applies.

jurisdictions.owner_gate: Hong Kong client status, active-marketing rules and provider licence scope must be verified.

market_data_compliance.rule: Market-data use rights are contract/licence questions independent of trading authorization.
canonical_handoff: P01-B already records UNKNOWN / CONTRACT REVIEW for unpublished rights.
P01-E must price and confirm exchange/index/vendor licensing and professional/non-professional classifications.
No public endpoint or free trial is presumed to grant redistribution or production non-display rights.

provider_broker_eligibility_checklist: Owner/entity jurisdiction verified by explicit Owner input
Regulator and licence/registration number verified on official register
Target product allowed for that client class
Crypto spot vs perpetual/futures/CFD classification verified
Automated/API trading permitted under provider terms
Account/entity type supports required API permissions
Withdrawal permission can be disabled or operationally isolated where supported
Market-data licensing permits intended internal/non-display/storage/derived use
Tax/reporting obligations flagged for professional review where necessary
Any product warning/knowledge/appropriateness assessment requirements satisfied
Evidence date and revalidation trigger recorded
decision_rules: Unknown jurisdiction or client class => provider/venue cannot be promoted to production baseline.
Conflicting provider terms vs regulator rule => FAIL_CLOSED and escalate to legal/compliance review.
Product unavailable to retail clients => do not attempt workarounds, offshore routing or status misrepresentation.
KYC/geofencing/provider eligibility controls must not be bypassed.
No automated process may change declared residency, client class or legal-entity facts.
Legal/compliance uncertainty blocks Live eligibility but does not block offline research using lawfully obtained data.

handoff.P01_E: Cost, licensing, data rights, professional/non-professional fees and contractual retention/redistribution rights.
handoff.P01_F: Primary/backup provider and broker design only among jurisdiction-eligible candidates.
handoff.P01_G: Provider baseline decision after jurisdiction + cost + rights + fallback evidence.
handoff.P03: Identity, secrets, audit, sanctions/KYC data handling and private administration.
handoff.P24: Fresh compliance/eligibility check before real-capital activation.

limitations: This matrix is representative, not exhaustive.
Rules and provider availability can change; revalidation is mandatory before account opening and Live/Canary progression.
National implementation and local regulator rules may be stricter than supranational baselines.
Tax treatment is explicitly out of scope for legal conclusions and requires jurisdiction-specific professional review when needed.
No conclusion is made about the Owner's actual legal eligibility.
